title: THE VANTAGE POINT OF THE ELDERS & FATHERS: THE CHILDREN ARE LISTENING

sense.text:
“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies” because we broke God’s laws. When we broke his laws we went into physical captivity, a physical assault on our bodies: the whips, the lynchings, the castrations. Those are physical damages on us, sent “against thee” by the Lord because he was angry with us.

“In hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness”: we would have to go to our enemies to eat, to our enemies for water, to our enemies for clothes. Don’t read past that. A nation with men in it is supposed to provide its own clothes, its own food and water and shelter. Why the hell do I have to go to another man to give me the things I am supposed to get for myself? That is a slap in the face, and it was put upon us to make us mad at the sight of what we see. When we look at the destruction and degradation of our people, it is supposed to drive us to anger. Anger is a good thing. That punk Christianity talk makes you afraid to be angry, but God gives you anger for a reason: anger gets ish done. Oppression makes a wise man mad enough to get off his ass and get things going.

“And in want of all things”: anything we need, we would have to get from our oppressors. And we come to socialize that as normal, to the point that when someone says we should do these things for ourselves, our own people say, why are we doing that, we got daddy white man to feed us. The mind is sick, and Christianity helped perfect that kind of thinking.

“And he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” The yoke of iron restrained us physically, but it had a psychological effect as well. It stayed on our necks until they said, give them Christianity. Once we accepted Christianity they said, you can let them go now, because now their spirits are in chains. They will never leave you, never want freedom, never want to provide their own clothes, food and water. The perfect breaking of us was done through that evil doctrine called Christianity. It destroyed our men, and once the men are destroyed the whole nation is destroyed. How could a woman look up to men that are destroyed? Men could see their women getting raped and it was not a problem. That is how we are now, and now many of us are doing it to each other. That is how sick we have gotten.

Christianity has done to the black mind what chattel slavery failed to do. In chains we still fought to get out; we kept breaking away from massa, killing his chickens and his hogs to get away, and we kept a semblance of pride and dignity. So another Edomite told the slave master to teach them religion, the perfect doctrine for a slave. The victims of Christianity think they are good members, but they are victims of white supremacy, sitting in the church hating themselves.

So it destroyed the will for us to do anything for ourselves. We have to break that curse and return back to the Most High, turn back to Christ. That is why Bishop Nathanyel began IUIC: not a carnal movement, but because our people need spiritual correction from the Bible. They need the commandments. Our minds and our thinking got sickened in slavery and have to be transformed, and the only thing that converts and transforms is the laws of God. The elders learned that and passed it down; we stand on their shoulders, which is really the shoulders of Christ, to take this gospel and fix our people.

Part of the elders’ job is to set up organizational foundations: foundations in our knowledge, resting on Christ as the cornerstone, but also literal buildings and institutions where people can see the works of the teaching. Tell someone in the street to repent and he will say, the gospel sounds great, but where is the sanctuary at? Where is your school, your institution? You can’t tell him to go to the internet. Back in 2015, when we dealt with the building in New York, the Bishop said any leader that is not forwardly thinking about building and directing institutions is a waste of time. As a man thinks, you are supposed to see some action from it. Let me see the fruits of your labor, not a whole life of nothing but words. And anything, women, men, friends, family, that threatens that, you separate yourself from it.

“What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?” Can words save him? Because that is all you are giving them. Faith alone just says, I believe in something. You can have faith in your head all day long, underneath your skull, but I can’t see it. The only way I will know what is in your mind is when I see action as a result of your thinking.

So if you have faith but no works to validate that faith, how can you say you have faith? There is no such thing as faith without its validation. You have faith in your head and you ain’t making no moves; it might as well not even be there. Faith is only validated by action. As a man thinketh, he becomes what he thinks, and once you see what he becomes you already know what was in his head.

The churches use faith like it is just a little thing: just believe in white Jesus. That ain’t going to get you nowhere but dead. Can faith alone save him? No.

“If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food”: James broke it all the way down to make it super simple. I got all the faith in my head, head about to burst open with it, but people are hungry. That faith can’t do a damn thing for them, because I have not taken it and materialized anything that can help that brother or that sister. That’s church. That’s Christianity. That ain’t the Israelites.

“Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled”: be warmed and filled with my words, I gave you great words. The man is still hungry and ain’t got nothing. “Notwithstanding” means it doesn’t mean any damn thing; it is not validated, there is no value to it. “Ye give them not those things which are needful to the body”: you tell them about all the great stuff, but where is the fruition of what you’re saying? Proper faith would have created something to actually help the brother or the sister.

That is what our people will say: how are you going to do all this preaching to me when you ain’t even done it for your own self, your own congregation, your own family? “What doth it profit?” Nothing comes out of it.

“Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.” That’s crystal clear. Faith does not exist if works are not attached to it. When anybody talks faith, faith, faith with no works behind it, they are not even telling you about faith; they are lying to you, they don’t have faith at all.

So our faith is demonstrated by maintaining institutions of learning, where our people are fed spiritually and also learn to take care of themselves physically, so that we are not destitute of food or of clothing, but take care of each other the way the elders had the brethren pool what they had extra at the apostles’ feet to take care of the body. Seek the kingdom and all these things will be added. The Lord who clothes the grass of the field and feeds the fowls of the air will take care of us; the real faith, if you believe it, makes stuff happen.

That is what the works of IUIC show: sisters teaching modesty, self-worth, marriage and broken homes to girls in Africa, and a young girl there fully engaged, listening. If we were just a group that talked about faith and no works, this word would never have got to her. All of the good works done all over are exactly because of the works. The faith we talk about is validated by the works you see in people changing their lives.

precepts.why:
Some people don’t even understand what faith really is. “Now faith is the substance.” Faith is a what? The substance. So don’t tell me you got faith: faith is the substance, and substance is what you can touch, something you can see, something materialized. Even if he or she has not achieved it yet, you can tell they are on their way by how they carry themselves.

On a college campus you see a student walking into the engineering building with his T-square and his architect tubes. He ain’t got the degree yet, he is not an architect or an engineer yet, but by the works you see, you can tell where he is going. That is how your faith is validated by your actions: even though you don’t have it yet, I can tell where you’re going because I can see how you’re thinking. Faith without works is dead, and where there is no vision the people perish.

You have to have a vision in your mind, and your mind has to manipulate the elements around you to form what you have in your head; when it comes to fruition you compare it to what is in your mind and say, it is good. That is what the Lord did. The earth was without form and void, not yet existing, and still he called it earth, because it existed in God’s mind. Then the spirit of the Godhead moved upon the face of the waters, the elements, and formed earth and then light, and he saw that the light was good. How could he say it was good unless he compared the light that was formed to what he imagined in his mind? Sisters do the same at the mirror: you don’t walk away until what you have done with your hands matches the image of yourself you had in your mind. That is the power we have, but because our elders were cut off from giving us basic understanding like that, we fell asleep for decades, for centuries.

“Of things hoped for.” If it is hoped for, can you see it? No. It is still a vision away from you, out of your immediate grasp. We hope for a kingdom; we hope to rule again. How do I know that is what you are hoping for? Because I see you operating mentally to get there. You’ve changed how you act, your posture, how you speak, how you dress, your whole persona, and people can see you’re not walking crooked like you used to walk. That is what the Lord wants from us.

“The evidence of things not seen.” How do I know what is evident in your life? By how you move. How do I know you are going to become a doctor, a physician, an architect, an engineer? The evidence is seeing how you are moving toward what you hope for. That is what faith is, and that is why, when James asks whether faith without works can save a man, he is not speaking of faith the way the churches use it.

sense.text:
While our brothers and sisters are inspired by our righteous examples and learn to function as a unified society, we wait, in quotes, for our deliverance from our Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ. “Therefore wait ye upon me, saith the Lord” gets thrown at us to keep us from making moves: don’t do nothing, get comfortable, sit back and just wait on the Lord. That ain’t what the Bible is talking about.

Wait “until the day that I rise up to the prey.” He is not telling you to wait to get your families together. He is not telling you to wait to build; Jeremiah tells you to build houses. He is saying, go ahead and build, and you wait till I kill your enemies, and by then you would already have learned how to be a nation. You can’t wait till the day the doors open for us to get into the kingdom. Your job is to practice nationhood now, to get it right now, while the Lord holds these nations off at bay and gets ready to strike them down. We don’t need to make moves, we don’t need to build, we don’t need to organize: I don’t want to hear that garbage.

“For my determination is to gather the nations, that I may assemble the kingdoms, to pour upon them mine indignation”: to put them all together and smash them. While I am getting set to destroy your enemies, I need you to learn how to operate as an organized nation now. Who will commit to your trust the true riches if you don’t even know how to deal right with each other now? That is what we are teaching our young men, and they are getting it. It makes our enemies mad, but the sisters are getting it and the brothers are getting it. Some struggle, and that is okay; we had to be worked on too. As long as you don’t bug out and do some foolishness where you have to be delivered to Satan, we will work with you.

“Even all my fierce anger: for all the earth shall be devoured with the fire of my jealousy.” Jealous of who? Of us, the Israelites. We are his children, and when a mother and a father are jealous over their children they will destroy every damn thing. The Lord is saying, I’m jealous over you, but I need you to operate as my sons and daughters, and while you get yourselves together I will take care of your enemies. Then, when he is smashing them all: come into the joy of thy Lord, you took the one talent and turned it into five, into ten, well done, go inherit five cities.

You can’t inherit nothing if you haven’t practiced it. If you haven’t rehearsed the righteous acts, you can’t set up nothing; give you five cities and you will turn them into debauchery and evil. Practice it now. Use the wisdom of the scriptures your elders and fathers are giving you, and make proper decisions about setting the nation up properly. Then you’re ready.

Our people built Black Wall Street in the 20s, and the whole purpose of terrorism, of an attack, is to break your spirit. But if your spirit can’t be broke, we keep on moving and we will rebuild. Imagine what we could have done if we never left that course, even with them attacking us. But this time we are set up so that when they come forward the next time, their ass is going to be laying dead on the ground. We don’t advocate violence on no level, but if somebody is looking to attack you, then with every fiber of your being make sure they don’t get to do it again to nobody else.

“If a thief be found breaking up, and be smitten that he die, there shall no blood be shed for him.” You ain’t did nothing wrong. That is where the castle doctrine and the self-defense laws come from: they got that from the Bible, our records. We are not talking about a weapons race; they have the bombs. But when it comes to protecting yourself, you have the right to do that by any means necessary.

That is not a call to go grabbing anything and looking for white folks. Don’t look for nothing. Get into this Bible and build your families up. But there needs to be a level of preservation for the nation. We have to protect what is ours.

precepts.why:
“But now, he that hath a purse, let him take it, and likewise his scrip: and he that hath no sword, let him sell his garment.” Christ said this to the disciples because he was going off the scene, and they were going to be left here to defend the gospel. Whenever they got attacked, they had better have some means to protect themselves.

That is the Bible, so the hell with what people think and what people say. I am going to follow what the Bible says, and I ain’t sorry for nothing the Bible says. The scriptures came right on time.

The hard times and the destruction of our nation have created strong men. The elders saw the degradation, we have seen it, and we are mad. Oppression doesn’t make a dumb man mad; it makes a wise man mad, wise enough to organize, to teach his children and his nation and get them all up out of the mud. Because of that our enemies come against us, and we are not supposed to just lie down and let them run over us.

sense.text:
Look at children of our people stealing in a grocery store, locked inside, cursing and threatening to break the door down. A mother and a father produced that. Because we don’t have laws, we don’t have guidance, this is what you get: marry the wrong man or the wrong woman and you will be getting up out of your bed to bail them out. If one believes in discipline and the other don’t, there is no accord, and that is unclean children. If you aren’t going to guide them up properly you should not have any. Whenever we walk away from the commandments of God, it evolves into this. The man and the woman both must hate sin, have a fervent disdain for what happened to our fathers and mothers, and not repeat it.

“Do not prostitute thy daughter.” If we are going to clean up this mess, we have to start with stuff like this, digging into the nuances of the words. Letting her listen to music she shouldn’t, be around crowds she shouldn’t, isn’t deep enough. Allowing boyfriends and girlfriends, promoting promiscuity and not giving her proper order is closer, because that leads to babies, no husband, all kind of foolishness. But there is a step before that: the parents allowing the attire. Once the attire gets on, the boyfriend stuff follows. Let your daughter go outside with her behind out, and that will produce nothing but damn problems; people kill over that.

That is exactly why the enemy goes after your daughters and your women and entices them: once you mess them up your children are done, because they are the ones with the kids. Even Willie Lynch said she is the most valued commodity, because once they mess her head up they can destroy the entire nation. The men out there just want a nut; they ain’t marrying her or doing nothing righteous with her, and she wants validation because her father ain’t nothing, while the mother tells her to go sell her ass by letting everybody look at it. Amongst those crowds are all kinds of sex offenders. At the parades the camps tell the young girls they should not be dressed like that, and it is the black woman who attacks the camp and calls us a cult, while a pedophile stands next to the camp; in one county there were 694 of them. At Mardi Gras in Mobile, Alabama, a woman of 65 turned and shook her behind in a diaper, and when she was told to put some damn clothes on she broke a bottle and turned to violence. People are upset at talk like this, but this is just talking about it, while you are actually living it, and your children are in this damn thing. You better be glad somebody is telling you about it.

“To cause her to be a whore.” When she gets whored out by all kinds of men, her value goes to the floor. She will lay with any man that smiles at her; her self-esteem is gone.

“Lest the land fall to whoredom.” Now you have a land of whorish women giving their bodies to just anybody, no scrutiny, no recommendations; all he has to do is say some sweet, enticing words. “And the land become full of wickedness”: no value, no scruples, no righteousness, everything about what feels good now. Full of wickedness literally means full of wickedness.

This is an example of a land full of wickedness, all because a mother and a father let the daughter dress like that and put her out there, switching her behind up and down: all these videos, OnlyFans and all of that. That drives men crazy in wickedness, not to do nothing righteous at all. “Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy”: controversy means against. The Lord is against how we live. “With the inhabitants of the land”: this is mainly speaking of the northern kingdom, but all of us are doing this now, so it is on everybody.

“Because there is no truth”: truth is the Bible, truth is the laws. Nobody in the land is adhering to the commandment not to prostitute thy daughter; nobody is paying attention, nobody is bringing that precaution in the land at all. “Nor mercy”: people get killed over this. Brothers have gone to jail and been shot down over it. “Nor knowledge of God in the land”: the knowledge of God is his commandments, which the priest’s lips are supposed to keep and the people are supposed to seek. They ain’t getting that knowledge at all.

“By swearing, and lying”: we heard complete lies two weeks ago, a man telling everybody that nobody told him to leave the sister alone, to make it look like the leadership didn’t know what was going on. The brothers had to stand up and correct him right there in front of everybody, so nobody would think he had a toe to stand on to justify the evil he did.

“And killing, and stealing”: we saw that in the videos. All of this because the woman was taught to let her behind hang out. The Bible gives a dress code: cover it. The Lord gave a dress code because he knows that if you rip your clothes off you are going to have all kinds of crap going on. David saw Bathsheba, and he lost it all.

“And committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood.” People get killed, stabbed, shot up, all because she got her clothes off in the street. Do you see the connection? That is what the Bible means by full of wickedness: the laws of God ain’t being taught, so there is no Bible, no scruples, no laws, and backdoor marriages produce madness like those children. We are not dealing with any of that. You will do it right or you won’t do it at all, and there will be no ceremony over fornication.

precepts.why:
The precept we always bring out: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” The law is the truth.

So when Hosea says there is “no truth” in the land, it means the laws of God are not being kept. Nobody in the land is adhering to the commandment not to prostitute thy daughter, and that is why the land is full of wickedness.

sense.text:
The brothers came into this gospel with all kinds of spiritual and psychological problems, from traumas and from how their families were, and the elders had to take those men in and build them up: teach them unity, teach them about being a man, about structure and discipline, how to ward off temptations. That is what was being done in the basement in the Bronx. Now people see thousands of brothers marching in the streets, men society had slated to be drug dealers, murderers, locked up, homos, baby daddies, and they can’t believe they are real men. Women cry and ask where these men came from. But they only see the final product, the tip of the iceberg: not the dedication, the hard work, the sacrifice, the failures, the splits, the decades it took.

That is David. “And every one that was in distress”: in the beginning stage of IUIC the men weren’t the full package. They came with problems, they came with issues. “And every one that was in debt, and every one that was discontented, gathered themselves unto him”: unto David. “And he became a captain over them: and there were with him about four hundred men.” All of them were men with issues; it wasn’t complete. All of us came into IUIC with issues.

precepts.why:
Look at those same men later: “thou knowest thy father and his men, that they be mighty men.” But were they mighty men at first? No. They are mighty men now because David taught them and trained them. David put a lot of work in them, the same way our leadership put a lot of work in us.

“And they be chafed in their minds, as a bear robbed of her whelps in the field.” They are men of focus. They ain’t bums no more, they ain’t childish no more; they are men of the Lord taking care of business. Back then there wasn’t that, and that is what you see now in the long lines of brothers in the street.

Some people are scared and surprised by this because they didn’t think we were this serious. You shouldn’t be scared; you should love it. We are serious, and we are not putting up with foolishness no more.

sense.text:
In the drills the Captain told the brothers there is no way a man should be able to break you by getting in your head; boys let men get in their heads. He was personifying sin: I’m trying to distract you, and you are supposed to say, I’m not moving, I’m not giving in to that temptation, I’m not entertaining that. Standing at attention you don’t get to scratch or lean, because you are hardening yourself not to be disturbed or distracted. That physical training transcends to the mental and the spiritual training, so that sinful impulses don’t take you off your mission. And when you move together and one brother steps out of line, everybody feels it: what you do affects everybody else. That is unity, one body, one face.

“Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.” This is what the brothers understood. Evil communications come to women and they come to men, and when they come you are supposed to shut that thing down, just like the Captain was bringing out. You don’t entertain it. It will corrupt your good manners, and the next thing you know you are caught up in some foolishness. Learn that discipline.

A father that came up through this will make sure his sons understand it, and make sure nobody gives his son feminine crap: let him deal with the men, so that when he grows up he can deal with a woman properly. That is not abuse. Some mothers are afraid to send their sons into something like this, thinking it is too rough for their boy. No: he needs to be in it, to be toughened up and start thinking like a man, so he doesn’t grow up and get tempted. When the men come up in proper discipline they are a real beacon of righteousness in the community. The fathers have spoken, and the children listened.
